**DK51* Ulcerøs colitis** is a World Health Organization (WHO)-classified diagnosis code utilized within the [[dansk-kvalitetsdatabase-for-inflammatoriske-tarmsygdomme|Dansk Kvalitetsdatabase for Inflammatoriske Tarmsygdomme]] (DANIBD) to identify patients with ulcerative colitis. It constitutes one of the two primary diagnostic categories that form the foundation for quality measurement, clinical benchmarking, and standardized coding within the national registry. 

In the 2023 DANIBD annual report, which covers detailed quality data from the period of October 1, 2022, to September 30, 2023, the DK51* code is used to illustrate the regional distribution of the disease. Patients diagnosed with DK51* Ulcerøs colitis accounted for 58% of all inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) patients in [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]], 55% in [[region-sjaelland|Region Sjælland]], 59% in [[region-syddanmark|Region Syddanmark]], 56% in [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]], and 60% in [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] [^src1]. This cross-regional data supports the national effort to systematize and improve IBD treatment through standardized coding and evidence-based development of treatment guidelines.

The diagnosis code continues to be tracked in the 2024 DANIBD report, where it appears in appendix tables detailing central quality indicators [^src2]. These indicators monitor critical aspects of IBD care, including the use of biological and small molecule drugs (Indicator 5), surgical interventions and reoperations (Indicator 6), and the epidemiological characteristics of patients with primary sclerosing cholangitis, a severe IBD comorbidity (Indicator 7) [^src2]. By tracking the DK51* code across these indicators, the registry maintains a detailed quantitative basis for quality monitoring and the development of treatment standards in Danish IBD care [^src2].
